databricks.titleIntro: Databricks is now a first-party provider
databricks.intro1: {{name}} is a custom provider pointing at a Databricks workspace. Bifrost now supports Databricks natively, with personal access tokens, OAuth service principals, Model Serving and AI Gateway routing. Your existing configuration needs to be migrated to the official provider.
databricks.intro2: Nothing changes until you confirm. You will see exactly what will be copied before the migration runs, and the custom provider is only removed after the new one is verified.
databricks.previewDesc: Review what will be migrated. Secrets are masked; anything that could not be read must be entered below.
databricks.runningDesc: Migrating. Keep this window open until it finishes.
databricks.loadErrorTitle: Could not read the custom provider
databricks.tokenUnread: The token could not be read from the custom provider.
databricks.tokenMasked: Stored secrets are masked and cannot be copied; enter it again.

firstParty.title: Official {{label}} integration available
firstParty.description1: We noticed you have a custom provider named
firstParty.description2: . Bifrost now supports {{label}} natively. You can delete the custom provider and add the official {{label}} integration from
firstParty.description3: , or keep using your custom provider as is.

configSheet.title: Provider configuration
configSheet.providerConfigurationsHelp: Configure which providers this can use and their specific settings. Leave empty to block all providers. Add providers to allow them.

allowedRequests.title: Allowed Request Types
allowedRequests.description: Select which request types this custom provider can handle.
allowedRequests.pathHint: Click the settings icon to customize endpoint paths or use full URLs.
allowedRequests.customPathDesc: Override with a path (e.g., /v1/chat) or a full URL (e.g., https://api.example.com/chat) to bypass base_url

keysForm.weightTooltip: Determines traffic distribution between keys. Higher weights receive more requests. Not used when adaptive load balancing is enabled - key selection is then based on live performance.
keysForm.copilotApiTokenDesc: Requires Network Config > Base URL set to the host the token was issued for, because a Copilot token does not carry one. Also expires after about 30 minutes, and Bifrost cannot refresh a token it did not mint, so prefer the GitHub App below for anything long-running.
keysForm.copilotTokenPlaceholder: Copilot API token, or leave blank to use a GitHub App
keysForm.allowedModelsTooltip: Select specific models this key applies to, or choose "Allow All Models" to allow all. Leave empty to deny all. Aliases must be added by their alias name - listing only the underlying model does not allow the alias (an alias best-model → gpt-4o requires "best-model" here, not just "gpt-4o").
keysForm.blockedModelsTooltip: Models this key must never serve. The denylist always wins - if a model appears in both Allowed Models and here, it is blocked. Select "All Models" to block every model on this key. Aliases are matched by their alias name - blocking only the underlying model does not block aliases that point to it.
keysForm.deploymentsDesc: Map a request model name to the provider's identifier (deployment name, inference profile ID, etc.). Expand a row for canonical name, model family, and provider overrides - these drive cost logs and family-based routing.
keysForm.deploymentsReplicateNote: Replicate deployments are listed only while "Use Deployments Endpoint" is on - otherwise type the owner/name and press Enter.
keysForm.useForBatchDesc: Enable this key for batch API operations. Only keys with this enabled will be used for batch requests.

azure.defaultCredentialDesc: Uses DefaultAzureCredential - automatically detects managed identity on Azure VMs and containers, workload identity in AKS, environment variables, and Azure CLI. No credentials required.
azure.scopesTooltip: Optional OAuth scopes for token requests. By default we use https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default - add additional scopes here if your setup requires extra permissions.

vertex.serviceAccountDesc: Uses the service account attached to your environment (GCE, GKE, Cloud Run). No credentials required.
vertex.workloadIdentityDesc: Exchanges the AWS identity attached to this workload (EKS IRSA or Pod Identity, ECS task role, EC2 instance profile) for a GCP token through a Workload Identity Pool AWS provider. No GCP service account key and no AWS access key required.
vertex.projectNumber: Project Number (Required only for fine-tuned models)
vertex.regionDesc1: Multi-region-only models are automatically routed to Google's matching multi-region endpoint. Turn on
vertex.regionDesc2: below to always use exactly this region.
vertex.forceSingleRegionDesc: Always call the region set above and skip automatic promotion of multi-region-only models to a multi-region endpoint. Enable when serving these models from a single region via provisioned throughput.
vertex.authCredentialsDesc: Service account JSON object or env.VAR_NAME
vertex.credentialsStoredSecurely: Credentials are stored securely. Edit to update.
vertex.wifAudienceDesc: The full resource name of the AWS provider in your Workload Identity Pool, shown as the audience in the GCP console.
vertex.impersonateSaTooltip: Leave empty to call Vertex AI as the federated principal directly (grant it roles/aiplatform.user). Set it to impersonate a service account that has the Vertex AI role; the federated principal then needs roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser on that service account.
vertex.tokenLifetimeDesc: Only used with a service account. 600 to 43200; the default is 3600.
vertex.awsRegionDesc: Region used to sign the STS request. Defaults to AWS_REGION, then instance metadata. Set it when neither is available in the pod.
vertex.awsRoleArnDesc: Assume this IAM role with the workload's credentials before the GCP exchange. Usually unnecessary: map the workload's own role in the pool provider instead.
vertex.apiKeyGeminiOnly: API Key (Supported only for gemini and fine-tuned models)

replicate.useDeploymentsEndpointDesc3: model on this key to /v1/deployments/{owner}/{name}/predictions, so plain model names stop working. To switch just one model, leave this off and set "Use deployments endpoint" on its row above.

vllm.serverUrlDesc: Base URL of the vLLM server (e.g. http://vllm-server:8000 or env.VLLM_URL)
vllm.modelNameDesc: Exact model name served on this vLLM instance

databricks.workspaceUrlDesc: Your Databricks workspace URL (e.g. https://dbc-1234abcd-5678.cloud.databricks.com or env.DATABRICKS_WORKSPACE_URL)
databricks.inferenceSurfaceDesc: Auto picks by model name: a dotted name such as system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5 goes to the Unity AI Gateway, anything else to Model Serving. Choose explicitly to pin one surface.
databricks.patDesc: Generate one from Settings > Developer > Access tokens in your workspace.
databricks.oauthDesc: Databricks recommends OAuth machine-to-machine for production. Tokens are minted from the workspace OIDC endpoint and refreshed automatically.
databricks.forwardTagsDesc: Sends the virtual key, team and customer names as Databricks-Ai-Gateway-Request-Tags, so Databricks usage tracking attributes spend the same way Bifrost does. Names only, never user identifiers.
databricks.clientIdPlaceholder: Service principal client ID or env.DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID

keyless.serverUrlDesc: Base URL of the {{server}} server (e.g. {{example}} or {{envVar}})

copilot.noteA: Copilot accepts either credential. Fill in
copilot.noteE: is the option for a shared gateway: usage bills to the organization that owns the installation and no individual Copilot seat is used. A
copilot.noteG: in the field above is simpler but expires after about 30 minutes, so it suits testing rather than a running gateway.
copilot.setUpGithubApp: Set up a GitHub App for Copilot
copilot.appCredentialsNote: Leave these blank if you supplied a Copilot API token above. Otherwise all four are needed together. The App needs the Copilot Requests permission at Read & write, installed on the organization that should be billed with All repositories access, and that organization must allow Copilot requests from GitHub App installations.
copilot.appIdDesc1: The GitHub App's App ID or Client ID, from its settings page.
copilot.installationIdDesc1: The installation on the organization that should be billed.
copilot.repositoryIdDesc: Any repository the installation can access. Copilot's permission check requires one in the token request even though the installation itself needs All repositories access, so this is not really a scoping choice.
copilot.privateKeyDesc: The App's private key in PEM form, as downloaded from GitHub. PKCS#1 and PKCS#8 both work.

anthropicEndpoints.label: Use Anthropic Endpoints
anthropicEndpoints.desc: Routes chat completions and responses requests through Anthropic-compatible endpoints.

bedrock.useOpenaiEndpointsDesc: Routes requests through Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoints instead of Converse.
bedrock.iamRoleDesc: Uses IAM roles attached to your environment (EC2, Lambda, ECS, EKS).
bedrock.bearerDesc: Uses a Bearer token for API key authentication.
bedrock.mantleProjectIdDesc: Scopes Bedrock Mantle-routed models (OpenAI-family / Gemma) to a specific project via the OpenAI-Project header. Leave empty to use the account's default project.
bedrock.assumeRoleArnDesc: Assume an IAM role before requests. Works with both explicit credentials and inherited IAM (EC2, ECS, EKS).
bedrock.externalIdDesc: Required by the role's trust policy when using cross-account access
bedrock.externalIdDescPeriod: Required by the role's trust policy when using cross-account access.
bedrock.batchRoleArnDesc: Service role Bedrock assumes for batch S3 access. When set, it takes priority over the role_arn sent in requests.
bedrock.mantleBearerDesc: Uses a Bedrock Mantle API key sent as a Bearer token.
bedrock.projectIdDesc: Scopes inference and model listing to a specific Bedrock project (sent as the OpenAI-Project / anthropic-workspace-id header). Leave empty to use the account's default project.

vpc.title: VPC Endpoints (Optional)
vpc.description: Route traffic through interface VPC endpoints instead of the public regional endpoints. Use each endpoint's DNS name from the VPC console, not its ID. Region is still required — it sets the request signing scope.

services.controlPlaneDesc: Serves model listing and batch jobs.
services.s3Desc: Serves batch file I/O. Requires the bucket-prefixed endpoint name. A Gateway endpoint needs no value here.

keysForm.azureGeminiNote: (Supported only for gemini and fine-tuned models)

apiStructure.baseProviderTypeDesc: The underlying provider this custom provider will use

betaHeaders.addPlaceholder: Add custom beta header prefix (e.g. new-feature-)
betaHeaders.knownHeaderError: This is a known header; use the override dropdown above instead
betaHeaders.invalidPrefixError: Prefix must contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens
betaHeaders.updateFailed: Failed to update beta header configuration

debugging.sendBackRawRequestDesc: Include the raw provider request alongside the parsed request in the API response.
debugging.sendBackRawResponseDesc: Include the raw provider response alongside the parsed response in the API response.
debugging.storeRawDesc: Persist raw request and response payloads in log records.

deployments.nameExists: A deployment with this name already exists.
deployments.draftHint: Both deployment name and model ID are required; this row will not be saved until both are filled.
deployments.canonicalNameHint: The canonical name used for routing and pricing. Defaults to the model ID when blank.
deployments.modelFamilyHint: Forces the family used for routing decisions. Derived from model name when left blank.
deployments.descriptionHint: Note for users. Not used by Bifrost.
deployments.descriptionPlaceholder: What is this deployment used for?
deployments.azureOverridesDesc: Override key-level Azure defaults for this deployment. Leave blank to use the key's settings.
deployments.apiVersionHint: Override the Azure OpenAI api-version query parameter.
deployments.anthropicVersionHint: Override the anthropic-version header for Claude-on-Azure deployments.
deployments.endpointHint: Point this deployment at a different Azure resource than the key default.
deployments.vertexOverridesDesc: Override key-level Vertex defaults for this deployment. Leave blank to use the key's settings.
deployments.regionHint: Multi-region-only models are auto-routed to a multi-region endpoint unless Force single region is on.
deployments.forceSingleRegionHint: Call the region above as-is and skip multi-region promotion of multi-region-only models. Use for provisioned throughput.
deployments.bedrockOverridesDesc: Override key-level Bedrock defaults for this deployment. Leave blank to use the key's settings.
deployments.inferenceProfileArnHint: Cross-region inference profile ARN to invoke instead of the model ID.
deployments.bedrockProjectIdHint: Scope this deployment's Bedrock Mantle (gpt-*/Gemma) calls to a specific project via the OpenAI-Project header. Leave blank to use the key's project.
deployments.bedrockMantleOverridesDesc: Override key-level Bedrock Mantle defaults for this deployment. Leave blank to use the key's settings.
deployments.bedrockMantleProjectIdHint: Scope this deployment to a specific project via the OpenAI-Project / anthropic-workspace-id header. Leave blank to use the key's project.
deployments.replicateOverridesDesc: Override key-level Replicate defaults for this deployment.
deployments.useDeploymentsEndpointHint: Route through Replicate's deployments endpoint instead of the models endpoint.
deployments.useAnthropicEndpointsHint: Route chat completions and responses requests through Anthropic-compatible endpoints.
deployments.providerOverridesDesc: Override key-level {{provider}} defaults for this deployment.

governanceTab.budgetNumberError: Budget limit must be a number
governanceTab.alignDesc: Reset budgets at the start of each period (e.g. 1st of month) instead of rolling from creation date. Quarterly budgets always align to fiscal quarter starts.

network.removeConfigError: You can't remove network configuration for this provider.
network.baseUrlRequiredError: Base URL is required for this provider.
network.streamIdleDesc: {{value}} Max time to wait for next chunk before closing a stalled stream
network.maxConnsDesc: Max TCP connections per provider host. For HTTP/2 providers (e.g. Bedrock), each connection supports ~100 concurrent streams.
network.keepAliveDesc: {{value}} Idle keep-alive for pooled connections. Set below the upstream server's keep-alive to avoid reusing connections it has already closed.
network.enforceHttp2Desc: Force HTTP/2 on provider connections. Relevant for net/http-based providers (e.g. Bedrock) where each HTTP/2 connection supports ~100 concurrent streams.
network.http2PingDesc: {{value}} Idle seconds before a client-initiated HTTP/2 keepalive PING. Prevents intermediaries from cutting quiet streams and long generations. 0 disables; requires Enforce HTTP/2.
network.allowPrivateDesc2: ). Required for providers on a LAN, k8s pod network, or private VPC. Cloud metadata addresses (169.254.x.x) are always blocked.
network.skipTlsDesc: Disable TLS certificate verification for provider connections. This bypasses server certificate validation and should be used only as a last resort when a trusted CA chain cannot be configured. Prefer ca_cert_pem for self-signed or private CA deployments.
network.caCertDesc: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for provider endpoint connections (e.g. self-signed or internal CA).
network.noChangesAndErrors: No changes made and validation errors present

pricingTab.ignoreCostDesc: Discard the cost the provider returns in its usage object and calculate it in Bifrost from model pricing and pricing overrides. Use this when a provider reports cost in its own units, such as credits or a non-USD currency. Models without pricing or an override are logged at $0.

promptCache.autoInjectDesc: Agentic clients such as Codex send no cache markers, so the cached prefix follows the newest message and every turn is billed as a cache write. Turning this on marks the first cacheable block instead, which keeps the cached region stable so turn 2 onward is a cache read. Requests that already carry their own cache markers are never modified, and models without explicit caching are left alone.
promptCache.ttlDesc: A longer TTL costs more per cache write but survives gaps between turns. Providers that cannot carry a TTL ignore this.
promptCache.injectionDesc1: Optional. Target specific messages instead of the first cacheable block. Adding any point
promptCache.injectionDesc3: the default strategy rather than adding to it. Each point needs a role, an index, or both. At most four markers are injected, matching the provider ceiling.
promptCache.pointError: Each point needs a role, an index, or both.

proxy.alert: Applies to HTTP requests and WebSocket-based Realtime/Responses connections. WebRTC-based Realtime sessions use a separate media path not covered by this proxy.
proxy.caCertDesc1: PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for TLS connections through SSL-intercepting proxies. You can also use

openaiConfig.disableStoreDesc: With the Responses API, store defaults to true, and when it is on, the generated response is stored for later retrieval via API. OpenAI exposes endpoints to retrieve and delete stored responses, so your response IDs become durable server-side objects instead of one-shot IDs.

webSearch.description: MCP tools added to every chat and responses request to this provider. Bifrost runs them itself when the model calls them and returns only the final answer. The model sees each tool under its name. A name that matches a tool the client sends replaces that tool, and the name web_search also replaces native web search.
webSearch.savedMissing: The saved MCP server "{{name}}" no longer exists. Pick another one.
webSearch.savedError: Could not load the saved MCP server "{{name}}".
webSearch.toolsError: Could not load this server's tools.

placeholders.empty: This MCP server exposes no tools

webSearch.noToolsInjected: No tools are injected for this provider.

keyForm.noPermission: You do not have permission to modify provider keys

oauthKeys.tokenUrlDesc: The identity provider's token endpoint. Must be https.
oauthKeys.privateKeyDesc: RSA or EC private key in PEM form. Bifrost signs each assertion with it.
oauthKeys.issuerDesc: The iss claim, usually the client or service account ID.
oauthKeys.subject: Subject (Optional)
oauthKeys.subjectDesc: The sub claim. Defaults to the issuer.
oauthKeys.audienceDesc: The aud claim, usually the token endpoint itself.
oauthKeys.keyIdDesc: The kid header, when the identity provider selects keys by ID.
oauthKeys.assertionLifetimeDesc: How long each signed assertion is valid for. Default 300.
oauthKeys.flowDescription: Bifrost requests an access token from the token endpoint, sends it as the bearer, caches it per credential and refreshes it before it expires. Use this for upstreams that issue short-lived tokens instead of a static key.
oauthKeys.audienceOptionalDesc: Sent as the audience form parameter, for providers that scope tokens by API.
oauthKeys.accountIdDesc: The Cloudflare account that runs Workers AI.

cloudflareMigration.title: Cloudflare is now a first-party provider
cloudflareMigration.intro1: {{name}} is a custom provider pointing at Cloudflare Workers AI. Bifrost now supports Cloudflare natively, and the name "cloudflare" belongs to the official provider, so this custom provider can no longer be edited. Your existing configuration needs to be migrated to the official provider.
cloudflareMigration.intro2: The provider is converted in place, so its keys, virtual key access, budgets and limits are kept, and nothing is deleted. Nothing changes until you confirm, and you will see what will change before the migration runs.
cloudflareMigration.reviewNote: Review what will change. Keys keep their stored tokens; anything that could not be read must be entered below.
cloudflareMigration.running: Migrating. Keep this window open until it finishes.
cloudflareMigration.loadErrorTitle: Could not read the custom provider
cloudflareMigration.accountIdHint: Read from the custom provider's base URL.
cloudflareMigration.noAccess: Migrating requires create and update access to providers.
